newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: BOBSLEIGH-IRISH PUSH FOR OLYMPIC GLORY.
newsitem.headline: BOBSLEIGH-IRISH PUSH FOR OLYMPIC GLORY.

text.p: There's not much snow in Ireland and little ice. There are few mountains and no Cresta run.
But when the bobsleigh competition gets underway at the Winter Olympics in Japan next year, an Irish sled will be at the starting line -- minus its practice wheels.
This follows the announcement that the International Olympic Committee's Solidarity Fund has committed itself to assisting the four-man Irish team to prepare for the Games in Nagano next January.
The cost of preparing the team for the trip is expected to cost 50,000 Irish pounds ($78,700) over the coming year.
"That would be to do the thing right while it might go to more if we were to buy some equipment rather than just leasing it out each year," team manager Pat McDonagh said.
